newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF says French bank competition intense in Q2.
newsitem.headline: BoF says French bank competition intense in Q2.

text.p: Competition over lending rates remained severe among French credit institutions during the second quarter of 1996, the Bank of France said on Wednesday in its quarterly financial survey.
"Competition among lending establishments continued to be particularly intense over lending rates and products," the central bank said.
Bank margins establised but at a weak level and an improvement in the financial situation of companies during the first quarter failed to carry over into the second quarter.

"The deterioration of operating profits and longer delays in settling bills led to cash flow difficulties and, for some, hardship in paying," it said. "This was no doubt the reason for a higher need for short-term credit."

Banks passed on the fall in interest rates to borrowers and savers, the survey found. The fall in rates led to major reallocations of savings into such areas as insurance products and housing savings plans.
